Probabilistic precedents acknowledged: Bayesian Maximum Entropy (multi-source drought fusion), copula-based scheduling (drought-to-irrigation), dynamic Bayesian networks (field-state tracking), multi-modal fusion networks
None of the reviewed probabilistic precedents couples all three capabilities (learned multimodal fusion + explicit probabilistic crop-water-state estimation + irrigation optimisation) end-to-end
Tomato is strongly responsive to irrigation management (both deficit and excess induce distinct stress responses)
RQ3/RQ4 coherence caveat: non-destructive physiological measurements (RQ4) validate crop-water-status component of RQ3 directly and root-zone soil-moisture component only indirectly
Probabilistic model families for posterior inference over latent variables from noisy multi-sensor inputs include Bayesian hierarchical models and Gaussian processes
FAO AquaCrop is an established, openly available, and well-documented crop simulation model

The honest uncertainty chain is the project's defining methodological commitment: uncertainty is propagated from observation through to the irrigation recommendation without collapse to a point estimate at any intermediate interface.
The diagnostic block is framed as a Bayesian inference problem computing the posterior P(field state | observations) over root-zone soil moisture and crop water status (RQ3).
Candidate model families for the probabilistic generative model include Bayesian hierarchical models and Gaussian processes.
Route B (homogeneous patch proxy) is the primary diagnostic implementation path (RQ2, operator-confirmed).
Route A (direct one-step probabilistic fusion) is implemented as a rigorous comparison baseline and committed fallback.
PlanetScope access secured via Planet platform and API (RQ8, operator-confirmed).
FAO AquaCrop crop model is used as the counterfactual simulation engine in the prognostic block.
AquaCrop is calibrated retaining a posterior distribution over parameters rather than a single maximum-likelihood point estimate (uncertainty-aware calibration).
The decision engine scores candidate irrigation decisions by expected water-use efficiency (WUE) under joint field-state and weather uncertainty (RQ6, operator-confirmed).

Assumption A1 (latent-state identifiability): the multi-sensor observation vector is informative about the latent field state. Tested by the WP3 validation protocol against the RQ5 calibration criterion.
Assumption A2 (Route B patch covariation): the proxy patch covaries with the target tomato crop in water-stress signatures at seasonal scale. Formally tested by a co-located seasonal campaign (RQ9).
Assumption A3 (AquaCrop adequacy for tomato): AquaCrop adequately simulates tomato crop growth and water use for the counterfactual irrigation comparisons the decision engine performs.

RISK-02 (spatial/temporal resolution harmonisation): rated probability high in the risk register. Mitigation: two-route architecture and sensor-appropriate QC pipelines.
RISK-03 (cloud limits optical; dense vegetation reduces SAR): rated probability high in the risk register. Mitigation: sensor weighting conditioned on acquisition conditions.
RISK-05 (Route B covariation not demonstrated): rated probability medium, impact high. Mitigation: pre-specified covariation test (RQ9); pre-committed Route A fallback.
RISK-06 (reported uncertainty not well calibrated): rated probability medium, impact high. Mitigation: RQ5 calibration criterion pre-specified before data collection.
RISK-07 (Route A too demanding): rated probability medium, impact high. Mitigation: Route B designated as primary path (RQ2); Route A as comparison/fallback.
RISK-08 (AquaCrop parameter overconfidence): rated probability medium, impact high. Mitigation: uncertainty-aware calibration retaining parameter posterior.
RISK-01 (PlanetScope access not secured) has been resolved before the fellowship begins: access is operator-confirmed as secured via Planet platform and API (RQ8).
